findings.statement: Certification is optional and comes after an app has been listed for at least six months with at least 60 active unaffiliated installs; it adds a 'HubSpot Certified App' badge and extra Marketplace visibility on top of a basic listing.
For a certification request, the Ecosystem Quality team responds within 10 business days, and the full review-and-feedback cycle should take no more than 60 days.

Certification requires the OAuth authorization code flow (no copy-pasted tokens, with the app managing and refreshing tokens itself), a verified domain, and a security questionnaire covering encryption, access controls, and token lifecycle management.
Listing an app triggers an initial Ecosystem Quality review within 10 business days; listing submissions are manually reviewed and rejected if they don't meet the criteria.
Only one app submission can be in process at a time; any additional app submitted while one is already being processed is automatically rejected.

Private apps are for a single HubSpot account and are created directly by an account admin, who sets its scopes; public apps use OAuth 2.0, are for use by multiple HubSpot accounts, and issue a refresh token alongside a 30-minute access token that your integration must store and renew.
You must be a super admin to access and create private apps in your HubSpot account.

Privately distributed OAuth apps can be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts (not including developer test accounts); unlisted Marketplace OAuth apps can be installed in up to 25 accounts until the app is listed.
Scopes can be required (must be authorized for install to succeed), conditionally required (only enforced when present in the install URL), or optional (never blocks installation).
Apps HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team hasn't verified show installers a warning banner, and HubSpot advises users to carefully review all scopes an app requests before installing.
Certified status is valid for two years on a rolling basis and must be renewed; HubSpot can also start recertification early if the app falls out of compliance.
Apps with a success rate below 95% across activities, or with fewer than three active installs, risk failing certification or being removed from the Marketplace.
Composio offers a managed HubSpot OAuth app by default, so a developer can skip registering their own; registering your own HubSpot app is mainly needed for custom branding or a private setup.
A certification request needs a demo video - without one, HubSpot won't review the app at all.

claim.text: Both private and public app creation are self-serve; a higher install cap exists for Solution Partners, but that's a benefit, not a requirement to participate at all.
Listing a public app triggers a mandatory Ecosystem Quality review, which responds within about 10 business days.
You must be a super admin to access and create private apps in your HubSpot account.
A private app is capped at up to 10 allowlisted accounts, and an unlisted public app is capped at up to 25 installs until it's listed.

tierReason.text: Listing a public app on the HubSpot Marketplace triggers a mandatory Ecosystem Quality review, with an initial response within about 10 business days and a full cycle that can take up to 60 days.

claim.text: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team gives an initial response within 10 business days, and the full review-and-feedback cycle should take no more than 60 days.

scopeForks.text: Using only an unlisted public app (never published to the Marketplace), Tier 1 applies: no mandatory HubSpot review, though the app is capped at about 25 installs and shows installers an unverified-app warning banner. Listing on the Marketplace - needed past that cap, and to remove the warning - moves it to Tier 2 with the Ecosystem Quality review described here.

claim.text: Composio offers a managed HubSpot OAuth app by default, so a developer can skip registering their own HubSpot app.

whatYouLose.text: On a managed app, the consent screen shows the platform's name and brand instead of yours, and scopes and rate limits are typically fixed rather than something you control.

whenToSwitch.text: Switch to your own HubSpot OAuth app once you need your own branding, a specific scope set, or a private (non-shared) setup.

flow.text: A developer creates a public app, configures required, conditionally-required, and optional scopes, and users authorize it through HubSpot's OAuth consent screen - optionally followed by Marketplace listing and review.

appTypes.text: Private apps use an access token and work in one account only; public apps use OAuth, can be installed across multiple accounts, and can optionally be listed on the Marketplace.

tokenNotes.text: Apps must handle OAuth token requests and refreshes themselves - users are never asked to copy and paste a code or token.

scopes.allows: Core data access the app always needs to function.
scopes.neededFor: Basic app functionality; install fails without these.

claim.text: Required scopes must be authorized for the app to install successfully.

scopes.scope: Optional / conditionally-required scopes (e.g. custom objects, Enterprise-only features)
scopes.allows: Access to features only some HubSpot accounts have, such as custom objects on Enterprise-tier accounts.
scopes.neededFor: Supporting higher-tier accounts without blocking installation for everyone else.

claim.text: Optional and conditionally-required scopes let an app support Enterprise-only features without blocking installs for accounts that lack them.

prerequisites.item: A public app (not a private one) if you need OAuth across multiple customer accounts

claim.text: Private apps are limited to one account and can't be listed; a public app is needed for multi-account OAuth.

prerequisites.item: A verified domain tied to your app

claim.text: Certification requires the app to use a verified domain.

prerequisites.item: A demo video (required only if you apply for certification)

claim.text: A demo video is required for a certification request - without one, HubSpot won't review it.

steps.title: Found HubSpot's app, listing, and certification docs
steps.detail: The research stage located HubSpot's public/private app overview and its listing and certification requirements.

claims.text: HubSpot documents private vs. public apps, Marketplace listing, and certification at developers.hubspot.com.

steps.title: Decide between a private and a public app
steps.detail: A private app only works in one account; a public app is needed for OAuth across customer accounts.

claims.text: Private apps work in one account only and can't be listed; public apps support multiple accounts via OAuth.

steps.title: Register a public app and configure scopes
steps.detail: Set your OAuth redirect URL and mark each scope required, conditionally required, or optional.

claims.text: Scopes are configured as required, conditionally required, or optional during app setup.

steps.title: Verify your domain
steps.detail: A verified domain is expected for certification and good practice generally.

claims.text: A verified domain is part of HubSpot's security expectations for an app.

steps.title: Build token storage and automatic refresh
steps.detail: Users must never be asked to copy and paste a code or token - the app has to manage and refresh tokens itself.

claims.text: The app must handle OAuth token requests and refreshes itself, with no manual token copy-paste step for users.

steps.title: Stay under the unlisted-app install cap, or prepare to list
steps.detail: An unlisted public app is capped at about 25 installs before you need to list it on the Marketplace.

claims.text: Unlisted public apps are capped at about 25 installs until the app is listed.

steps.title: Draft your scope justification
steps.detail: Use the Scope justification helper to prepare reviewer-facing notes for each scope you request.

steps.title: Draft a reviewer test plan
steps.detail: Use the Reviewer test plan helper so HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team can exercise the app quickly.

steps.title: Submit your app listing for Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: Only one app can be in review at a time; a second submission while one is pending is automatically rejected.

claims.text: Listing submissions go through a manual Ecosystem Quality review and are rejected if they don't meet the criteria.

steps.title: Respond to review feedback
steps.detail: The full review-and-feedback cycle should take no more than about 60 days.

claims.text: HubSpot's review-and-feedback cycle should take no more than 60 days.

steps.title: Listed on the HubSpot Marketplace
steps.detail: Once review passes, the app is listed and can connect real customer accounts without an install cap.

steps.title: Optional: apply for certification once you qualify
steps.detail: Needs 6+ months listed, 60+ active installs, and a demo video; adds a security questionnaire and a 'HubSpot Certified App' badge.

claims.text: Certification requires being listed for 6+ months with 60+ active installs, plus a demo video and security questionnaire.

provider.what: Reviews a Marketplace listing submission within about 10 business days, with the full cycle taking up to 60 days; optional certification afterward adds a security questionnaire and vulnerability assessment.

claims.text: Ecosystem Quality reviews listing submissions within about 10 business days, up to 60 days total.

customerAdmin.who: A HubSpot super admin on the customer's account
customerAdmin.what: Must be a super admin to access or create a private app; a public-app install typically also needs a user with sufficient permissions for the requested scopes.

claims.text: You must be a super admin to access private apps in your HubSpot account.

endUser.who: The HubSpot user installing the app
endUser.what: Authorizes the app through HubSpot's OAuth consent screen; an unverified (unlisted) app shows an extra warning banner.

claims.text: Users are advised to carefully review all scopes an app requests, and unverified apps show a warning banner.

stuckPoints.reason: Listing submission rejected or returned with feedback
stuckPoints.fix: Review Ecosystem Quality's feedback carefully - the full cycle can take up to 60 days, and only one submission can be in process at a time.

claim.text: Only one app submission can be in process at a time; a second one made while the first is pending is automatically rejected.

stuckPoints.fix: Submit your app for Marketplace listing once you approach the roughly 25-install cap on unlisted public apps.

claim.text: Unlisted public apps are capped at about 25 installs until the app is listed.

whileYouWait.text: An unlisted public app can be installed on up to about 25 accounts (or a private app on up to 10 allowlisted accounts) while you're building or waiting on listing.

keepsComingBack.text: Certified status must be renewed - it's valid for two years on a rolling basis, and HubSpot can trigger recertification early if the app falls out of compliance.
